title: OpenJDK accelerated Base64 decoding can corrupt memory on affected x86-64 processors
summary: Crafted Base64 input can cause an out-of-bounds write in the accelerated decoder. AWS identifies x86-64 processors with AVX-512 VBMI as affected; native Graviton workloads are not affected.

severity.rationale: Remote unauthenticated input can corrupt runtime memory, but requires the affected processor feature and decoder path. This is conditional exposure, not every Java deployment.

affected.note: AWS identifies specific fixed Corretto builds for release lines 17, 21, 25 and 27. Compare the complete build with the bulletin; other Java distributions need their own mappings.

exposure: Applications must decode attacker-controlled Base64 using the affected intrinsic on supported x86-64 hardware. AWS describes affected OpenJDK code from 17.0.6 onward.

params.instructions: Check Amazon Corretto version and whether the documented exposure conditions apply.

remediation.action: Update or contain the affected component
remediation.details: Install the fixed Corretto build for the release line and restart Java applications. AWS documents -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics as an interim mitigation.
remediation.risk: Medium. Updates can interrupt workflows and require compatibility checks.

verification: Check the running JVM build, hardware prerequisites and intrinsic setting after restart.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.
